title: upgrade attention kernels: flashattentionv2 + fused-qkv + rope/rotary optimizations
author: Daniel Park
description: Motivation: Improve single-request latency and throughput for medium/long context LLMs by upgrading to FlashAttentionV2 kernels, adding fused QKV/linear fused ops where beneficial, and improving rotary/rope handling to reduce kernel launches and memory traffic. This PR implements a kernel-selection layer that chooses between legacy kernels, FlashAttentionV2, and a new fused-qkv path depending on model shape, dtype, and hardware capability. It also introduces a rope/rotary precomputation path that reuses cached positional rotations across the KV cache to reduce re-computation during continuous batching. Performance: internal perf runs on A100 (80GB) show ~18-35% throughput improvement for long-context workloads (4k-32k) and 8-15% median latency reduction for 2k-8k ranges when using FlashAttentionV2 + fused ops vs previous runtime. Memory pressure is reduced by up to 10% for GPT-style models due to fewer intermediate allocations. Changes: 1) Add FlashAttentionV2 CUDA kernels and wrapper with fallback to FlashAttentionV1 for devices that lack required SM. 2) Add fused-qkv path that fuses linear(qkv) + split + transposition where beneficial; has autotune flags and fallback. 3) Rope/rotary optimization: cache pre-rotated cos/sin tables and reuse across KV cache entries; add fast path when sequence bucketing is stable. 4) Scheduler tweaks: improved continuous-batching decision logic to prefer model-variant with lower latency SLO; introduce a micro-batch aggregator to reduce kernel launch overhead for high-concurrency, short-seq workloads. 5) Tests and benchmarks: new perf harness scenarios, unit tests for numerical parity against reference kernels, and integration tests covering KV cache correctness across rollouts. Backcompat and rollout: the new kernels are feature-flagged with runtime.auto_kernel_upgrade = "opt-in" initially and gated by canary rollout. We added a runtime flag to force legacy behavior for customers needing deterministic binary parity. QA: numeric tolerances validated against reference implementation (max l2-diff < 1e-6 for fp16 in typical cases). We also stress-tested KV cache correctness under continuous batching and preemption. Rollout plan: canary on internal Dedicated cluster (10% traffic) for 1 week, then gradual ramp to 100% if perf/quality monitors are green. Related: ENG-2314 (perf initiative), SUP-4421 (customer incident re: rotary memory).
